chunks: From him, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Jew and the Christian, if they testify and then convert to Islam, their testimony is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a convert from Judaism or Christianity valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Sakuni from Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies that the prior testimony of a Jew or Christian is legally valid (jaizat) upon their conversion to Islam, resolving debates on whether their pre-conversion acts are retroactively accepted. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that conversion purifies the individual's status for legal purposes, ensuring continuity in their evidentiary value. This ruling is particularly significant in the context of *tahdhib* (purification) of witnesses, emphasizing that the new faith validates their previous standing in the eyes of the law.
